body: The commit-failure window on PR 205 is closed. Head now 5a4b0150, fast-forward on 761ebb35, 821 passing.U+000AU+000AReachable deterministically without touching production code. store.commit ends at casUpdateRef (src/store/write-path.ts:205), which shells out to git update-ref refs/logbook/ledger. Git's files ref backend takes its lock by exclusively creating refs/logbook/ledger.lock inside the repo's .git, so pre-creating that file makes git exit 128 with "Unable to create ... File exists".U+000AU+000ATwo properties make that usable rather than merely a failure. The message matches neither branch of CAS_MISMATCH_PATTERN (src/store/ref.ts:10), so the failure classifies as io rather than ref-moved and the retry loop never runs: one attempt, one refusal, no timing dependence. And the pointer store is a separate temp root from the repo's .git, verified by printing both paths at runtime, so breaking the ref leaves state/active-thread.json fully writable for the following park_thread. That separation is why the fixture works at all.U+000AU+000ARejected alternatives, each with a reason: store.commit's ops seam at src/store/records.ts:283 is unreachable because commit calls writeRecords with four args and no ops; GIT_DIR and GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY injection is dead because both sit in FORBIDDEN_ENV_KEYS and are stripped before every spawn; chmod on .git/objects was unnecessary once the lock worked and carries a restore obligation the lock does not; exhausting the ref-moved retry loop needs concurrency, which was excluded as luck-based. No filesystem permission was changed anywhere, so nothing needed restoring, and every probe removed its temp roots in a finally with the removal verified.U+000AU+000ANew case close.a-commit-failure-leaves-the-pointer-so-park-can-still-record at test/spawn/close.test.ts:335-408. It pins the literal refusal text "the ledger commit for this closure did not complete; retry the call.", unique to close_thread.ts:79 — the six sibling tools each name a different noun, and wholeRecordCapRefusal shares the thread field but no message text — so no other refusal can satisfy it. Then the pointer still names the thread and park_thread succeeds with parked_thread_ids equal to [threadId] and one session entry, proving the outcome was written rather than merely acknowledged. The unlinkSync sits in a finally before any assertion, so a failed assertion cannot wedge a lock file in the temp repo.U+000AU+000AThe mutation that matters fired: moving releasePointerIfOwned from line 147 to immediately above store.commit at line 136 turned it red with the assertion naming the ordering rule directly. That is exactly the position the earlier case could not reach.U+000AU+000AOne honest weakness the lead reported rather than hid: the no-lock control went red on an ENOENT from teardown rather than on an assertion, because the finally runs before the assertions and with no lock written the unlink throws first. It proves the fixture step is load-bearing, but the ordering evidence is the mutation, not the control.U+000AU+000AThe earlier case close.a-refused-closure-leaves-the-pointer-so-park-can-still-record is untouched and stays, because it covers the hoist-to-top position the new case does not. No test was weakened, skipped or deleted. concurrent.distinct-ids passed in 4426ms in the full run.U+000AU+000AOpen bookkeeping on 205: its body carries a verified line reading 820 passed, now 821, and describes two cases where there are three. Held pending the release engineer's answer on whether pr-create converges against an existing head, since the centralized tool exposes only pr-create, pr-close and compare, and hand-editing a body would make the caller the author of markup the tool is supposed to own.
